answer: The falcon graph is rebuilt each epoch, which means the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the jade audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 4 times its size, so a group of 15 keys loses far more than 15 single identities would. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the mesa checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. That is 31 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
